Article 29 UAE labor law includes several leave categories. These vacations are designed to address certain situations that may impact worker accessibility or productivity at work. Below are a few of the special leave categories:

Sabbatical Paid Leave

Sabbatical breaks, like annual leave, are compensated time off from employment. However, unlike annual leave, only Emirati employees are entitled to this leave. The sabbatical leave is typically associated with academics. However, it serves distinct purposes. 

Educational Leave

Most employees, regardless of industry, want to advance in their careers. Continuing studies and personal growth are effective approaches for ensuring continual upward advancement, and workers in the UAE may follow this path as well. According to labor legislation, employees with at least two years of service can take 10 working days each year to appear for tests at verified UAE educational institutions. 

Compassion Paid Leave

Death is a grief and painful occurrence that has a considerable effect on the emotional and physical health of individuals who are related to the departed ones. As a result, the UAE employment legislation allows employees to take time from work to mourn and make cremation or funeral preparations. In the event of a spouse’s death, it is five days, and the rest have three days from the day of death incident.

Pilgrimage and Umrah Leave

Pilgrimage is one of the most essential pillars of religion Islam, and every Muslim must experience it at least once throughout their lives. Islamic authorities see the pilgrimage as the most important expedition and a legitimate cause to take time from work in the UAE. 

According to the UAE’s government official portal, private-sector manpower in UAE are allowed to take a maximum of thirty days off for the pilgrimage, which is unpaid and provided only once throughout their employment. 

Please Note:

While Pilgrimage leave is mandated by law, Umrah does not have similar restrictions. Workers contemplating Umrah must either take an unpaid vacation or reduce the days from their yearly leave.

Child Births, like funerals, are metamorphoses that have an impact on a parent’s emotional and physical health. It’s especially noticeable in women who suffer from critical conditions like hormone imbalances and anxiety. The UAE labor rules provide for sixty days of paid maternity leave for female workers, with forty-five days at full salary and fifteen days at half compensation.  

If childbirth problems occur, an extra forty-five days of unpaid leave are allowed. Similarly, if the infant is unwell or disabled, the employer may provide a paid Thirty-day leave with the option to extend it for another thirty days without pay. 

Parental Paid Leave

In a progressive move aimed at emphasizing its regional leadership, the UAE implemented parental leave, becoming the first Arab country to allow this leave.
The UAE labor legislation provides parents of newborn babies with a five-day fully compensated leave, which should be taken within six months of the child’s birth.

The UAE labor law provides paid days off for national holidays specified by the government. Employers must compensate employees who work on certain holidays. This is accomplished by either providing a day off or paying at least 150 percent of the base compensation for the day. 

Paid Leave For Illness

Workers in the UAE are entitled to a maximum of ninety days of sick leave each year, with full compensation for the first fifteen days. The following thirty days are half-paid, with the last forty-five days unpaid.
To acquire paid sick leave, workers must notify their company within three working days of being unwell and present acceptable medical evidence.

Article 43 UAE Labour Law: What Should You Know?

Picture you are knee deep in a major project, your workforce is running as a well-oiled machine, and suddenly, a key worker hands in their resignation. Just like that, your manpower planning takes a hit. Sound familiar? Article 43 of UAE labour law comes to your rescue in this scenario.

Labour laws exist to create fairness. But they also shape how businesses like yours can effectively manage workforce transitions. Article 43 deals with resignation and termination as it sets clear rules on notice periods. This guarantees that neither employer nor employee is left without relevant resources.

What does it really mean for businesses that rely on manpower outsourcing services in UAE? Understanding Article 43 UAE labour law and relevant regulations help you avoid workforce disruptions, maintaining operational stability.

Key takeaways:

  • Article 43 UAE Labour Law: What does it say?
  • The Fine Print of Quitting: Why Article 43 UAE Labour Law Matters?

What Is Article 43 of UAE Labour Law?

At its core, Article 43 UAE Labour Law dictates the resignation and termination notice period for employees under unlimited contracts. Here’s the gist:

  • Employees should give their employer a written notice before resigning
  • The standard notice period is 30 to 90 days, depending on the employment contract
  • Employers should also provide the same notice period when terminating a worker’s contract
  • If either party skips the notice, they must pay compensation equal to the wages for the notice period

This law keeps operations on track for companies hiring blue collar workers in construction, manufacturing, logistics, and industrial sectors. A sudden exit without a proper notice would disrupt your workforce, negatively affecting your project deadlines. That’s why having a solid manpower outsourcing strategy in place is key in these situations.

Article 23 of the UAE Corporate Tax Law covers rules on exempt income, detailing cases where businesses are not subject to corporate tax.

Article 23 offences generally refer to violations under specific UAE laws, such as misuse of natural resources or breaches in corporate tax compliance, depending on the legal context.

Article 23 of the Limitation Act states that in cases of fraud or mistake, the limitation period begins when the fraud or mistake is discovered.

Article 44 UAE Labour Law 2026: Complete Termination Guide

Employers and employees must understand their rights in the UAE business environment. For this, the UAE Labor Law is designed. The law regulates relationships between employees and employers. An assurance of fairness and protection for both parties. One such section of the law is article 44 UAE Labor Law. It outlines the grounds that an employer can terminate an employee without providing prior notice.

The updated version of this article is designed to safeguard employers’ interests. At the same time, it promotes a transparent working environment. Both parties can guarantee that their rights are upheld. They need to understand the core principles of this law. In turn, disputes are minimized. A productive and respectful working relationship is maintained.

What is article 44 of the UAE Labor Law?

Article 44 of the UAE Labor Law empowers employers. It gives them the authority to terminate an employment contract. They do so without providing a notice period under certain circumstances. Specifically, these circumstances are outlined in the law. Designed to protect employers from employees who engage in severe misconduct/actions. Those activities could harm the business or disrupt the workplace.

Note that the law does not allow employers to terminate employees arbitrarily. They cannot dismiss employees without a legitimate reason. Thus, it prevents unfair termination practices. Emphasizing that termination without notice should be based on specific situations. This protects employees from any random dismissal.

Article 43 UAE Labor Law states safety and protection for employers and their workers. You must know them to get assistance when your laws are violated.

Key grounds for termination under Article 44 UAE Labor Law

Article 44 of the UAE Labor Law specifies several situations. In these situations, an employer can terminate an employee’s contract without providing notice. For termination, the following table summarizes the key grounds:

Ground for Termination Description
Fraudulent Documents Submission of fake documents, forged certificates, or false identity information.
Material Loss Causing significant material loss to the company due to negligence or recklessness.
Deliberate Damage Intentionally damaging the employer’s property or equipment.
Criminal Activity Involvement in criminal acts. This includes assaulting a coworker or employer. It can be verbal or physical.
Safety Violations Participating in activities. Those violate workplace safety regulations.
Abandonment Absence from work without providing a valid reason/notice.
Breach of Confidentiality Unauthorized disclosure of company information. Those that can be regarded as sensitive.
Refusal to Follow Instructions Repeated refusal to follow job instructions. Including contractual duties.

These grounds ensure that employers can take swift action. Specifically in the event of severe misconduct. Failures to maintain workplace order and discipline. This protects the company’s assets and reputation.

Employer’s responsibilities under article 44

Employers also have specific obligations under Article 44 of the UAE Labor Law. To ensure a legally sound and just dismissal, employers must:

  1. Notify MOHRE (Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization): Employers must report the termination to MOHRE within seven working days of the incident. Failure to do so could weaken the employer’s case, especially in the event of a dispute.
  2. Provide evidence of misconduct: Employers must provide the employee’s misconduct proof or breach of employment terms. Showing that dismissal is legitimate and justified.

Article 29 of UAE Labor Law also protects the rights of both parties. Gain insights on this to be aware of your rights and obligations.

Employee rights and protections

Article 44 UAE labor law protects employers. Also, it includes measures to safeguard employees’ rights. The law ensures that:

  1. Fair treatment: Employees cannot be dismissed arbitrarily. They do not terminate without a valid reason. As per law, workers are not subject to unfair/discriminatory termination practices.
  2. End-of-service benefits: Workers completing over a year of service are entitled to gratuity. It is also called end-of-service manpower employee benefits if their employment is terminated. Note that the gratuity amount is calculated based on the service length and the employee’s last salary.
  3. Right to challenge termination: Workers can file a complaint with MOHRE if they believe their dismissal is unfair. The ministry will then investigate the matter if the dismissal is found to be unjustified. Resulting, the employee may be reinstated or compensated.

Article 44 and annual leaves in UAE

Workers are entitled to annual leave benefits under Article 44. Employees who have completed at least one service year are entitled to 30 days of paid leave annually. Employers must respect this right. In case of termination occurs, the employee’s contract must also consider this leave entitlement.

Article 44 and working hours in UAE

UAE labor law also outlines provisions related to working hours and conditions. Key points include:

  • Working Hours: The standard working hours should not exceed. Not more than eight hours per day or 48 hours per week.
  • Rest Periods: Adequate rest periods must be provided. This includes weekly days off.
  • Health and Safety: Employers must create a safe and healthy working environment for their employees. They must provide protective equipment if the work involves hazardous conditions. So that safety regulations are followed.

title: Article 45 UAE Labor Law: Updated Guide 2025
content:
Published On: March 29, 2025Updated On: January 30, 2026

Article 45 UAE Labor Law: Updated Guide 2025

Article 45 UAE Labor Law outlines the situations under which a staff member may end the employment agreement without delivering the normal notice period. In case of any violations, harassment, or unlawful practices, workers may quit immediately without any notification. The legislation requires employees to report such infractions to MOHRE within certain deadlines. Employers may end the job contract in certain conditions from workers at the workplace.

In simple terms, Article 45 gives legal relief for individuals who are experiencing serious workplace challenges, guaranteeing that they are not imprisoned in abusive or illegal working arrangements.

Understanding Article 45 UAE Labor Law 2025

The UAE Labour Law Article 45 allows workers to end their contract of service without notice in certain crucial situations. These situations often entail employer wrongdoing or contract violations.

Major factors include an employer’s inability to meet contractual or legal responsibilities, as well as an employee being assaulted or subjected to severe abuse at work. The legislation seeks to safeguard from unfair or dangerous working conditions for manpower supply in Abu-Dhabi or any other Emirates.

Workers must report such infractions to MOHRE within a specific time range. This article offers critical legal protection, allowing employees to walk away from abusive conditions without incurring the fines associated with traditional contract dismissal.

End of Employment: Modifications of Labor Law for Dismissal

End-of-Employment with Notice

Despite the most recent changes to UAE labor law, businesses may terminate workers for a ‘legitimate reason.’ Fixed-term hiring agreements cannot be canceled before the end of their term, with the exception of summary termination, without payment. 

Article 29 of UAE Labor Law states workers are entitled to thirty working days of fully compensated annual leave after one year of employment, which can be used during the notice period.

The legislation governing worker termination for any logical or legitimate reason stays unchanged until 2025. The expiry of a fixed-term job agreement acts as legal grounds for dismissal. Workers on fixed-term labor contracts can now be terminated on notice as usual, with no further compensation required. Exploitation, or terminating an employee for submitting a complaint against their company, is illegal.

End-of-Service without Notice Period from the Employer

According to Article 44 UAE labor law, a company can dismiss a staff member without notice if they adopt a fake identity, submit counterfeit papers or certificates, commit an error that causes significant material loss to the company, or intentionally damage the employer’s property. Note that an organization must notify MOHRE about the occurrence within seven days of becoming aware of it.

  • If a staff member violates security guidelines or fails to perform fundamental responsibilities under the employment contract, they may face dismissal if they continue to do so. Additionally, if they reveal any secrets of the company, the employer may suffer losses or miss out on opportunities.
  • If a worker violates guidelines concerning the safety of employees and the precise location of the business, given that such directions were published in writing in obvious places or spoken advised to an uneducated worker.
  • A worker is discovered to be intoxicated or under the influence of illegal narcotics during working hours or does an activity that violates public morality in the workplace.
  • A worker attempts to harm his superior, manager, or any of his coworkers while on the job.
  • An employee leaves without a valid explanation for over twenty inconsistent days or more than seven consecutive days in a year.
  • An employee uses his position of authority illegally to achieve personal goals and manpower employee benefits. 
  • An employee joins a different company without following the relevant norms and legal protocols. 

The legislation states that an employer can dismiss without notice only after completing a formal investigation concerning the worker. The termination notice must be in writing, legitimate, and properly handed over to the worker.

End-of-Service without Notice Period from the Employee

  • According to Article 45, a worker may cancel the agreement without notice if the company fails to satisfy his contractual or statutory responsibilities to the worker, given that the employee notifies the MOHRE fourteen working days preceding the date of resigning, and the employer fails to fix the infraction after being advised by the MOHRE of the same.
  • If the employer harassed or tormented the worker while at work, provided that that individual informed the appropriate authorities and the MOHRE within five working days of the incident of the date he was available to report.
  • If the employer directed the employee to perform a task completely distinct from the work agreed in the contract of hire without the worker’s written consent and express authorization, except in cases when labor is essential.
  • Despite knowing the threats, the variables that represent a serious risk to the workers’ security and health were not removed. Article 26 specifies situations involving significant hazards at work.

Changes for Notice Period Regulations

The current UAE labor code 2025 for manpower in UAE still requires thirty days of notification for workers who have finished their probationary term. However, an authorized notice period of ninety days has been set.
Employees departing while still working under endless term contracts must provide an appropriate notice period of:

  • Thirty days of leave for workers with up to five years of employment.
  • Sixty days of notice for staff members with five to ten years of employment.
  • Ninety days for workers with at least ten years of working tenure.

Critical Conditions for Employment Contract Dismissal: New Updates

The following are the scenarios in which an employment contract may be terminated under Article 42 of the supervision of employee relations in the private sector if the term of the contract expires and is not extended or renewed.

  • If the company and worker collaboratively agree in writing to dismiss it.
  • If any party decides to discontinue it, given that the party quitting follows the termination requirements of the contract of hire and the notification period agreed upon.
  • In the case of the employer’s death, if the subject matter of the contract is tied to its entity. 
  • In the case of the employee’s death or complete permanent incapacity to work, based on a declaration provided by a medical authority.
  • Where an employee confronts a final court verdict of a freedom limitation consequence for a term of at least three months.
  • If the enterprise is permanently shut down, in line with the laws established in the UAE
  • If the employer declares bankruptcy or insolvent or confronts any economic or extraordinary circumstances that impede the ongoing execution of the project. 
  • If the staff member fails to meet the standards for renewing the work permit due to reasons beyond the employer’s control. 

Notification Period for the End-of-Contract

According to Article 43 UAE Labor Law, any party in the job agreement may end the relationship for any ‘legitimate cause,’ provided that:

The opposite party receives written notification, and the dismissing party provides a notice period of one to three months. Furthermore, the following conditions must be complied with the task agreed upon in the agreement must be completed within the notice period. The worker has the right to receive his full salary as per the contract throughout the notice period.

The party that fails to fulfill the notice period must pay the other a specific allowance equivalent to the employee’s salary for the whole notice period or in proportion to the balance of the duration. The notice period payment is computed based on the worker’s last salary.

If the employer cancels the agreement, the employee has the right to receive one day of unpaid leave weekly throughout the notice period to look for another employment.

It should be noted that the notification time may be decreased or waived by an understanding between the two parties, with no violation of any of their rights.

Final Words

The new employment regulations definitely consider the need for the highest ethical standards in employment practice and manpower supply in Sharjah or any other Emirates. It seeks to promote optimal industrial advancement and labor market efficiency. The new labor regulation is a significant step toward balancing the interests of both employees and employers.

FAQs

What is Article 45 of the UAE Labour Law? And how does it work?

Under Article 45, employees can resign immediately if employers seriously violate labour obligations.

When can an employee resign without serving notice under Article 45?

Workers can resign instantly if employers fail to pay wages, abuse workers, or breach contract terms.

What employer violations are covered under Article 45?

Article 45 violations include unpaid salaries, unsafe work conditions, forced labour, or contract manipulation.

Does resignation under Article 45 affect gratuity or benefits?

Workers retain full end-of-service benefits if Article 45 applies legitimately.

Can an employer take action against an employee under Article 45?

The employer can’t take action if the employee proves employer violations through MOHRE or legal channels.

What documents are required to apply to Article 45?

The key documents required are salary records, complaint filings, inspection reports, messages, or MOHRE case references.

The legislation governing worker termination for any logical or legitimate reason stays unchanged until 2025. The expiry of a fixed-term job agreement acts as legal grounds for dismissal. Workers on fixed-term labor contracts can now be terminated on notice as usual, with no further compensation required. Exploitation, or terminating an employee for submitting a complaint against their company, is illegal.

End-of-Service without Notice Period from the Employer

According to Article 44 UAE labor law, a company can dismiss a staff member without notice if they adopt a fake identity, submit counterfeit papers or certificates, commit an error that causes significant material loss to the company, or intentionally damage the employer’s property. Note that an organization must notify MOHRE about the occurrence within seven days of becoming aware of it.

  • If a staff member violates security guidelines or fails to perform fundamental responsibilities under the employment contract, they may face dismissal if they continue to do so. Additionally, if they reveal any secrets of the company, the employer may suffer losses or miss out on opportunities.
  • If a worker violates guidelines concerning the safety of employees and the precise location of the business, given that such directions were published in writing in obvious places or spoken advised to an uneducated worker.
  • A worker is discovered to be intoxicated or under the influence of illegal narcotics during working hours or does an activity that violates public morality in the workplace.
  • A worker attempts to harm his superior, manager, or any of his coworkers while on the job.
  • An employee leaves without a valid explanation for over twenty inconsistent days or more than seven consecutive days in a year.
  • An employee uses his position of authority illegally to achieve personal goals and manpower employee benefits. 
  • An employee joins a different company without following the relevant norms and legal protocols. 

The legislation states that an employer can dismiss without notice only after completing a formal investigation concerning the worker. The termination notice must be in writing, legitimate, and properly handed over to the worker.

End-of-Service without Notice Period from the Employee

  • According to Article 45, a worker may cancel the agreement without notice if the company fails to satisfy his contractual or statutory responsibilities to the worker, given that the employee notifies the MOHRE fourteen working days preceding the date of resigning, and the employer fails to fix the infraction after being advised by the MOHRE of the same.
  • If the employer harassed or tormented the worker while at work, provided that that individual informed the appropriate authorities and the MOHRE within five working days of the incident of the date he was available to report.
  • If the employer directed the employee to perform a task completely distinct from the work agreed in the contract of hire without the worker’s written consent and express authorization, except in cases when labor is essential.
  • Despite knowing the threats, the variables that represent a serious risk to the workers’ security and health were not removed. Article 26 specifies situations involving significant hazards at work.

Changes for Notice Period Regulations

The current UAE labor code 2025 for manpower in UAE still requires thirty days of notification for workers who have finished their probationary term. However, an authorized notice period of ninety days has been set.
Employees departing while still working under endless term contracts must provide an appropriate notice period of:

  • Thirty days of leave for workers with up to five years of employment.
  • Sixty days of notice for staff members with five to ten years of employment.
  • Ninety days for workers with at least ten years of working tenure.

Critical Conditions for Employment Contract Dismissal: New Updates

The following are the scenarios in which an employment contract may be terminated under Article 42 of the supervision of employee relations in the private sector if the term of the contract expires and is not extended or renewed.

  • If the company and worker collaboratively agree in writing to dismiss it.
  • If any party decides to discontinue it, given that the party quitting follows the termination requirements of the contract of hire and the notification period agreed upon.
  • In the case of the employer’s death, if the subject matter of the contract is tied to its entity. 
  • In the case of the employee’s death or complete permanent incapacity to work, based on a declaration provided by a medical authority.
  • Where an employee confronts a final court verdict of a freedom limitation consequence for a term of at least three months.
  • If the enterprise is permanently shut down, in line with the laws established in the UAE
  • If the employer declares bankruptcy or insolvent or confronts any economic or extraordinary circumstances that impede the ongoing execution of the project. 
  • If the staff member fails to meet the standards for renewing the work permit due to reasons beyond the employer’s control. 

Notification Period for the End-of-Contract

According to Article 43 UAE Labor Law, any party in the job agreement may end the relationship for any ‘legitimate cause,’ provided that:

The opposite party receives written notification, and the dismissing party provides a notice period of one to three months. Furthermore, the following conditions must be complied with the task agreed upon in the agreement must be completed within the notice period. The worker has the right to receive his full salary as per the contract throughout the notice period.

The party that fails to fulfill the notice period must pay the other a specific allowance equivalent to the employee’s salary for the whole notice period or in proportion to the balance of the duration. The notice period payment is computed based on the worker’s last salary.

If the employer cancels the agreement, the employee has the right to receive one day of unpaid leave weekly throughout the notice period to look for another employment.

It should be noted that the notification time may be decreased or waived by an understanding between the two parties, with no violation of any of their rights.

Final Words

The new employment regulations definitely consider the need for the highest ethical standards in employment practice and manpower supply in Sharjah or any other Emirates. It seeks to promote optimal industrial advancement and labor market efficiency. The new labor regulation is a significant step toward balancing the interests of both employees and employers.

FAQs

What is Article 45 of the UAE Labour Law? And how does it work?

Under Article 45, employees can resign immediately if employers seriously violate labour obligations.

When can an employee resign without serving notice under Article 45?

Workers can resign instantly if employers fail to pay wages, abuse workers, or breach contract terms.

What employer violations are covered under Article 45?

Article 45 violations include unpaid salaries, unsafe work conditions, forced labour, or contract manipulation.

Does resignation under Article 45 affect gratuity or benefits?

Workers retain full end-of-service benefits if Article 45 applies legitimately.

Can an employer take action against an employee under Article 45?

The employer can’t take action if the employee proves employer violations through MOHRE or legal channels.

What documents are required to apply to Article 45?

The key documents required are salary records, complaint filings, inspection reports, messages, or MOHRE case references.

How to Avoid Hiring Mistakes With UAE Manpower Firms in 2025?

In today’s whirlwind hiring landscape, particularly in a dynamic economy like the UAE’s, choosing the right manpower firm can either turbocharge your growth or throw you into a costly talent tailspin. With 2025 bringing sweeping changes in employment norms, tech integration, and global workforce trends, hiring isn’t just a task anymore — it’s an art form. To avoid hiring mistakes, businesses must look beyond the surface and evaluate manpower firms with a sharper, more strategic lens.

And yet, far too many companies still trip up — lured by polished brochures or flashy promises — only to discover that the agency they trusted has misfired, mismatched, or completely misunderstood their needs. Sound familiar? In this blog, we’re unraveling how to get it right: uncovering how to sidestep those classic (and not-so-classic) hiring mistakes when working with UAE manpower firms in 2025. Let’s dive in and make your next hire your best hire.

Why UAE Manpower Firms? Why Now?

The UAE is a talent magnet. From tech specialists in Dubai to hospitality wizards in Abu Dhabi, companies are looking to scale fast and smart. Manpower agencies play the middlemen (and women), streamlining sourcing, vetting, and onboarding. But here’s the twist: Not all manpower firms are cut from the same cloth. Some deliver gold. Others? Pure glitter.

Before we dive into how to avoid hiring misfires, let’s look at the current landscape.

Snapshot: Manpower in UAE Trends in 2025

AI-powered candidate filtering is faster but sometimes biased or surface-level. The freelance workforce surge is a need for flexible contracts and short-term hires. Skill-first hiring culture in which credentials matter less and practical skills matter more. Emiratization compliance focuses on hiring local talent in key sectors.

Red Flags: How to Avoid Hiring Mistakes in UAE?

The most common hiring blunders often masquerade as “reasonable choices.” Here’s what to actively steer clear of:

1. Picking the First Agency You Find on Google

It’s tempting to go with the top search result. But visibility doesn’t always equal credibility. You need to dig deeper. Don’t hire based on pretty websites or generic promises like “100% Satisfaction.” Always consider reviews, referrals, or past client results.

2. Overlooking Industry Specialization

A manpower supply in a Sharjah firm that sources construction workers may not understand the nuances of hiring cloud engineers or vice versa. Always ask Do you specialize in our industry? Can you show hiring success in similar roles?

3. Ignoring Contract Clarity

Ambiguity breeds disaster. From service charges to candidate replacement policies, your contract should be as clear as crystal. Look for clauses that cover candidate trial periods, free replacements, and refund policies.

Top 7 Tips to Avoid Hiring Mistakes with UAE Manpower Firms

Here’s your go-to guide for hiring smart and avoiding the trapdoors.

1. Vet the Vetter

Before you let a firm filter your future employees, make sure you filter them. Must ask who conducts your interviews, AI tools, or industry experts? Can you share screening criteria or assessment templates? A reliable agency won’t shy away from transparency.

2. Demand Real Success Metrics

Fancy words mean nothing without data. Always look into the placement success rate. It reveals actual effectiveness. Client retention rate is another important aspect. If the rate is high, it means high satisfaction and reliability. Check the time-to-fill average, which shows efficiency in delivering candidates.

3. Understand Cultural Fit

The UAE is a cultural melting pot. One-size-fits-all hiring won’t cut it. Ask if the agency considers cultural adaptability, soft skills, and work ethic when recommending candidates, not just credentials.

4. Test Their Tech Stack

If the manpower supply in Abu Dhabi firm is still emailing spreadsheets back and forth, it’s 2023 tech in a 2025 world. Must look for ATS (Applicant Tracking System) integration, skill-assessment platforms, and AI interview analysis tools. Bonus points if they give you dashboard access to monitor hiring in real-time.

5. Avoid Lock-In Traps

Some agencies sneak in exclusivity clauses, minimum hire commitments, or hidden renewal fees. Red flag if you’re charged for candidate resumes. There’s a “finder’s fee” even for short-term roles. They restrict you from working with other agencies

6. Prioritize Local Labor Law Knowledge

With frequent labor law updates in the UAE. Especially around Emiratization and visa reforms, ignorance isn’t bliss. It’s a lawsuit waiting to happen. Ensure your agency keeps up with MOHRE guidelines and knows sector-specific hiring compliance. They should know how to handle visa sponsorships ethically

7. Ask for Customized Solutions, Not Cookie-Cutter Lists

A good firm will tailor solutions to your company’s vibe and vision. A bad one will just flood your inbox with resumes. Look for agencies that offer employer branding support. Opt for the one who creates customized onboarding frameworks and provides post-placement follow-ups

Checklist: Choosing the Right UAE Manpower Firm

Check

Industry specialization

✅

Transparent pricing

✅

Custom recruitment approach

✅

Local compliance understanding

✅

Post-hiring support

✅

Positive client testimonials

✅

Scalable talent solutions

✅

Final Thoughts: Smart Hiring is Strategic Hiring

Hiring the right manpower firm in the UAE isn’t just about avoiding mistakes. But it’s about building partnerships that fuel your business growth.

Remember, in a region as ambitious and competitive as the UAE, talent is currency. And who you entrust to handle that currency makes all the difference.

So, question boldly. Analyze deeply. Choose wisely. Because when you pick the right firm, you don’t just fill a vacancy, you elevate your entire operation.

Look out for hybrid agencies offering “human + AI recruitment.” These are emerging as the sweet spot—tech-driven efficiency plus the nuanced judgment only people can provide.

Ready to Hire Smarter in the UAE?

Ng Manpower has a strong name in the list of those who are offering skilled and talented manpower in the UAE. We have proudly announced our achievements that have helped employers to employ only the best talent. We know what it takes to hire the perfect candidate while leveraging our full potential. The Ng Manpower team never compromises on quality, and thus, we avoid those mistakes that most big names in the market are making.

However, before starting with us, it’s your right to ask the right questions. Demand clarity. And remember, we never hire mediocre candidates who often come from rushed decisions. Great hires come from sharp partnerships, as we are doing! Start today with confidence! Contact us today to get more information.

Companies can use structured interviews, verified agencies, skill assessments, and proper documentation to avoid bad hiring decisions.

Background verification prevents fraud, fake credentials, and compliance risks.

Employers should watch for inconsistent work history, unverifiable references, false documents, and unrealistic salary demands.

Manpower agencies pre-screen candidates, verify documents, and maintain legal compliance.

Before finalizing a hire, employers should check visa eligibility, qualifications, references, contract terms, and compliance status.

title: 7Benefits of Accounting Temporary Staffing for Your Business
content:
Published On: February 17, 2025Updated On: November 3, 2025

7 Benefits of Accounting Temporary Staffing For Your Business

It can badly disrupt operations when a business experiences an unexpected surge in workload. Sometimes, a key team member from the finance department is unavailable. Thus, we’ve all faced situations where a temporary solution is needed. To fill the gap that’s where accounting temporary staffing becomes invaluable! Businesses meet short-term accounting needs with this flexible solution. This provides immediate support without the hassle of committing to full-time hires.

This blog will explore the:

  • Key benefits of temporary accounting staffing.
  • The process of utilizing temporary staff.
  • How working with staffing agencies can streamline your financial operations.

What is accounting temporary staffing?

Hiring professional accountants on a short-term basis is termed accounting temporary staffing. The purpose behind this is to meet specific business needs. Typically, these staffing solutions are sought during periods of high demand, such as tax season, special projects, or employee absences.

Temporary accountants can handle various financial duties. These may include:

  • Bookkeeping
  • Financial Reporting
  • Tax Preparation
  • Auditing
  • Payroll processing

Having Accounting temporary staff means that your financial operations continue smoothly. You are free from the long-term commitment of hiring full-time employees.

How do accounting temporary staffing agencies work?

Staffing agencies, specializing in accounting professionals. They provide businesses with temporary accounting staff when needed. These agencies handle the hiring and onboarding process. As a result, businesses have skilled accountants to fill short-term gaps.

Generally, the process works like this:

1. Understanding your needs

The agency will first consult with your business to understand the specific accounting needs. Be it for a:

  • One-off project
  • Tax season
  • Covering an employee’s leave

Agencies will gather all the necessary details about the skill set required. This could involve bookkeeping, tax preparation, and financial reporting.

2. Recruitment and screening

The staffing agency taps into its pool of accounting professionals once the job description is clear. They screen and assess candidates based on skills, certifications, and experience. Agencies verify references and perform background checks to ensure you receive highly qualified staff. Their manpower recruitment process is seamless. The aim is to fill the position with the right talent as soon as possible.

3. Placement and onboarding

The agency handles the placement and onboarding process after matching the right candidate. The temporary staff will be integrated into your team quickly. This way, you may face minimal disruption to your daily operations.

4. Ongoing support

Many agencies provide continuous support during the temporary staffing period. If you need to adjust the staff size or extend the contract, the agency will manage those changes on your behalf, offering you the flexibility you need.

Hire manpower supply companies in UAE if you need a quick solution. They are experienced in finding the right candidate that fits well in the role.

Types of accounting temporary staffing

Temporary accounting staffing can be customized. Based on the unique needs of your business. For instance, some common types include:

1. Short-term staffing

Short-term staffing is perfect for filling immediate gaps. Caused by unexpected events like:

  • Employee absences
  • Sick leaves
  • Increased workload

Short-term staffing ensures your operations run smoothly without hiring a full-time employee.

2. Project-based staffing

Project-based staffing offers you professionals with precise knowledge. Quite effective when you need accounting expertise for a specific project. From system implementation to year-end reporting, or financial audits. This type of staffing provides the expertise to meet your goals within a set timeframe.

3. Seasonal staffing

Seasonal accounting staffing is ideal for businesses. Those experience predictable fluctuations in workload, such as:

  • During tax season

Published On: November 18, 2024Updated On: October 20, 2025

Benefits of Hiring a Manpower Consultancy in Abu Dhabi

When it comes to sourcing the right talent for business growth, companies in Abu Dhabi turns to manpower consultancy that offers many benefits for their support. Working with a trusted manpower consultancy benefits in Abu Dhabi means gaining access to qualified professionals who understand the specific needs of your industry. In a growing market, securing the right talent maintains a competitive edge. And that’s exactly where manpower consultancies come into play. 

These are the takeaway points from this article on the upsides of Abu Dhabi manpower consultancy.

Local market requirements – what local expertise can do in your favor?

A reputable manpower consultancy in Abu Dhabi knows the ins and outs of local labor market. With their deep knowledge of industry trends and demands, these consultancies are quick in identifying the best talent for any given role. They understand the importance of manpower in Abu Dhabi’s growing sectors. This helps them bring specialized expertise in matching businesses with skilled candidates.

Understanding local labor laws

Following labor regulations is necessary in Abu Dhabi. Every reliable Abu Dhabi manpower consultancy ensure that companies remain compliant. They guide them with all necessary requirements. This reduces the risk of non compliance. it in turn leads to smoother operations.

  • Industry-specific recruitment

Different industries have their certain requirements. Manpower consultancies in Abu Dhabi are quite the experts in these specifics. They identify candidates who possess the skills as well as the cultural and professional mindset suited for your field.

A Wider talent pool — how gaining access to talent is possible with this collaboration?

A major advantage of hiring a manpower consultancy Abu Dhabi is access to an extensive network of professionals. Consultancies have databases full of candidates ready for various roles. This makes it easier to find the right match for a company’s specific needs.

  • Extensive network of candidates

Manpower consultancies maintain relationships with professionals across sectors. This network includes local as well as international talent. They expand the possibilities for businesses to find suitable employees without prolonged search times.

  • Targeted talent search

Consultancies use refined tools to screen candidates. This helps with confirming that only those who truly meet the criteria are shortlisted. This process saves businesses valuable time and resources by presenting only the most qualified candidates.

  • Quick fulfillment of labor needs

Be it permanent staff or temporary labor supply in Abu Dhabi that a company requires, manpower consultancies are quick in responding to these needs. That’s due to their extensive reach in the workforce.

Reduced recruitment time and costs

The hiring process is time consuming and expensive for companies lacking dedicated recruitment teams. Partnering with a manpower consultancy in Abu Dhabi can be a huge help in reducing recruitment timeline and associated costs.

  • Efficient process management

Consultancies simplify each phase of hiring. This saves companies the effort and expense involved in managing these tasks on their own.

  • Reduced training time

With their expertise, manpower consultancies match businesses with candidates who already possess the required skills. It cuts down the time and cost of training new employees.

  • Lower risk of hiring errors:

As they thoroughly vet candidates, manpower consultancies lower the chances of mismatched hires. This often results in added costs and disruptions.

Abu Dhabi’s labor regulations — labor laws & compliance

In a country with strict UAE labor laws, compliance is all the more important for companies. Manpower consultancies are experienced with these regulations. They make sure that all recruitment practices are up to local standards.

  • Legal compliance and documentation

They handle necessary documentation. This assists businesses avoid potential fines and legal issues that arise due to violations

  • Work visa and permit support

Consultancies assist in processing work visas and permits. It makes certain that your employees can legally work in Abu Dhabi without complications.

  • Ongoing advisory services

Many manpower consultancies provide advisory services that keep companies updated on any regulatory changes. This aids companies in remaining compliant with new laws.

Short term and long term hiring — what flexibility means for your recruitment needs?

Whether a business needs short term, project based staff or long term employees, manpower consultancies provide flexible solutions. They understand the fluctuating demands of the local market. This in turn lets them adjust hiring plans accordingly.

  • Temporary staffing for projects

For projects with specific deadlines, consultancies provide temporary staffing solutions. This way companies have the right manpower when they need it. They do not have to commit to long term contracts.

  • Scalable recruitment

As companies expand, their staffing needs change. Manpower consultancies offer scalable recruitment solutions. These grow with your business. It allows you to adjust your team size as needed.

Improved employee retention rates

Finding the right talent is only part of the equation. Retaining that talent maintains a productive workforce. Manpower consultancies prioritize matching candidates with roles that match their skills and career aspirations. This leads to higher satisfaction and retention.

  • Matching skills and career goals

Understanding candidates’ career goals let’s consultancies place employees in roles that genuinely fit their aspirations. This improves job satisfaction and retention.

  • Continuous employee engagement

Many consultancies follow up with employers and employees to address any issues early on. This guarantees smooth working relationships and minimizing turnover rates.

  • Positive work environment

Through curated recruitment solutions, manpower consultancies assist with promoting a productive work culture. That’s because they ensure the selected candidates resonate well with your company’s values and objectives.

Enhancing Abu Dhabi’s workforce quality

Working with a manpower consultancy contributes to the growth and quality of your local workforce. Confirming that companies hire the right people, manpower consultancies indirectly support the overall development of Abu Dhabi’s business scene.

  • Developing local talent

Many consultancies focus on training and upskilling local candidates. This ends up creating a skilled labor pool that benefits Abu Dhabi’s industries. It also contributes to the city’s economic development.

  • Bridging skill gaps

With insights into market trends, consultancies bridge skill gaps by identifying specific competencies that businesses require. They guide companies to candidates with those skills.

  • Promoting sustainable employment

By matching candidates with the right jobs, consultancies play a role in building long lasting careers. This results in a more strong and reliable workforce.

In summary: how NG Man Power as a manpower consultancy can transform your business

In Abu Dhabi, finding and retaining the right talent is necessary for your business growth. Partnering with us, a manpower consultancy in Abu Dhabi, offers you a structured approach to hiring. This means you can focus on your business’ core operations instead. Meanwhile, leaving recruitment to be handled by our team of experts. With industry insights, a broad network and our knowledge of local labor requirements, NG Man Power gives way to a smooth hiring process. One that saves time and resources for your company.

There’s more to hiring a manpower consultancy than a hiring solution. It’s a partnership that supports the goals of your business in the long run. Our manpower consultancy is equipped to meet your needs.

Published On: March 24, 2025Updated On: November 3, 2025

Bereavement Leave UAE 2025 | Updated Labour Law Guide

Losing a loved one is an emotional storm no one is ever truly prepared for. But in moments of grief, the last thing anyone should worry about is work obligations. That’s where bereavement leave UAE comes into play. The UAE labor law acknowledges the importance of time off to cope with such losses, offering structured leave benefits to employees.

If you’re wondering how much time you’re entitled to, who qualifies, and whether your job security is affected, you’re in the right place. This guide will break it all down in simple terms, ensuring you get the most updated insights for 2025.

Bereavement leave in UAE: understanding your entitlement

As per the UAE Labour Law, employees working in the private and public sectors are entitled to bereavement leave when a close family member passes away. The number of days depends on the relation to the deceased:

  • 5 days for the loss of a spouse
  • 3 days for the loss of a parent, child, sibling, grandchild, or grandparent

This leave is fully paid, meaning there is no salary deduction when you take bereavement leave in UAE. However, leave must be taken within a set period following the death.

Who can apply for bereavement leave in UAE?

To qualify, an employee must:

  • Have a valid employment contract in the UAE
  • Provide official proof of the loss (such as a death certificate)
  • Inform their employer within the stipulated time

It’s important to check with your HR department on the specific documentation required, as different companies might have varying internal policies.

Bereavement leave in UAE for private sector employees

The UAE labor Law extends bereavement leave rights to both public and private sector employees. While public sector employees follow government-set guidelines, private companies may have additional policies in place. Some firms allow additional unpaid leave or flexible work arrangements during this period.

For expats working in the UAE, the process remains the same. However, companies may grant extra unpaid leave if the death occurs abroad and the employee needs to travel.

Bereavement leave in UAE for family and expats

Losing a family member is a heartbreaking experience, and the UAE labour law acknowledges this by offering leave to help employees manage personal and emotional responsibilities. Whether you are a UAE national or an expat, you are entitled to bereavement leave under the same conditions.

Family relations covered

The UAE labor law recognizes the importance of time off when losing immediate family members. The law covers spouses, children, parents, siblings, and grandparents. However, if an employee loses a more distant relative, additional leave may depend on company policies.

Bereavement leave for expats

For expats living in the UAE, bereavement leave applies just like it does for UAE nationals. If an expat employee needs to travel to their home country, additional unpaid leave may be arranged at the employer’s discretion.

Bereavement leave in UAE calculator: how to plan your time off

Many employees ask: How many days can I take off? To simplify, use the table below:

Relationship to Deceased Paid Leave (Days) Additional Unpaid Leave (Employer’s Discretion)
Spouse 5 days Yes, if approved by the employer
Parent 3 days Yes, if approved by the employer
Child 3 days Yes, if approved by the employer
Sibling 3 days Yes, if approved by the employer
Grandparent/Grandchild 3 days Yes, if approved by the employer

If you need extra days, discuss with HR about emergency leaves in UAE or unpaid leave options.

How does bereavement leave compare to other leave types in UAE?

If you’re trying to understand how bereavement leave compares to other types of leave, here’s a quick breakdown:

  • UAE labor law annual leave: Employees receive 30 days of paid leave per year, separate from bereavement leave.
  • Maternity leave in UAE: Female employees are entitled to 60 days of maternity leave, with a portion being fully paid.
  • Sick leave UAE: Employees get 90 days of sick leave per year, with varying pay structures.
  • Emergency leaves in UAE: Some employers offer emergency leave, but it is usually unpaid and granted on a case-by-case basis.
  • Unpaid ;eave policies: Some companies offer unpaid leave extensions for those who require additional time to handle personal responsibilities after a loss.

Latest trends: is bereavement leave evolving in UAE?

As we step into 2025, UAE labor laws continue to evolve with employee well-being in mind. Some recent trends include:

  • More compassionate HR policies: Many firms are expanding their policies to allow extra unpaid leave.
  • Flexible work arrangements: Some companies now permit remote work or flexible hours after bereavement leave.
  • Mental health support: Employers are focusing on grief counseling services for affected employees.
  • Extended Support Networks: Organizations are introducing employee assistance programs (EAPs) to help workers cope with loss through counseling and wellness programs.

NG Manpower – your trusted HR partner

At NG Manpower, we understand that employees are the backbone of every business. Whether you’re an employer looking to update your company’s bereavement leave policies or an employee seeking guidance on your rights, our HR experts are here to help.

From managing annual leave, maternity leave, sick leave, and emergency leaves in UAE, to optimizing workforce solutions, we’ve got you covered. Our team ensures seamless HR compliance, helping businesses create a compassionate and productive workplace. Get in touch today and let’s build a workplace that truly cares.

Final thoughts

Grieving is a personal process, and having the right bereavement leave in the UAE allows employees the necessary time to cope. Whether you’re an expat or working in the private sector, understanding your rights is essential. As UAE labor laws continue to evolve, staying informed helps both employees and businesses build a compassionate work environment. A well-defined leave policy enhances workplace well-being, loyalty, and productivity. Contact us now to learn more.

Common Questions about Bereavement Leave in UAE

Can I extend my bereavement leave?

Yes, but it depends on your employer. Some companies allow additional unpaid leave upon request.

What if I lose someone outside my immediate family?

Bereavement leave is officially granted for close family members. If you need leave for a distant relative, it will be your employer’s discretion.

Is bereavement leave separate from sick leave or annual leave?

Yes, bereavement leave is a separate entitlement and does not affect your sick leave or annual leave balance.

title: Blue Collar Workers in UAE
content:
Published On: April 3, 2024Updated On: November 10, 2025

Blue Collar Workers in UAE – Impact on Economy

In the vast fabric of the modern workforce, blue collar workers in UAE often take a back seat to administrative professionals in the spotlight. But the importance of workers should not be taken lightly. These hardworking people are the backbone of the industries that grow our economy. Maintain our infrastructure and keep society running smoothly.

In this article we will discuss the differences that blue collar manpower in Dubai receive and the rest of the UAE. We will explain in detail about the minimum wage differences and the fundamental roles within it. The working conditions in which blue collar workers UAE work and their legal rights.

Wage Disparities Among Blue Collar Workers

Blue collar workers in UAE are the backbone of our society, yet they are often ignored and undervalue. These hardworking people keep our cities functioning and our infrastructure and economy thriving. The resilience and strength of the working class, despite many hardships and often harsh working conditions, is truly remarkable.

Despite the rising cost of living, wages in many jobs have stagnated or grown more slowly than in other industries. This wage stagnation makes it difficult for workers to meet their basic needs and support their families.

Role of Industry and Sector in Wage Differences

One of the biggest problem for blue collar workers in UAE is the loss of jobs. As automation and technological advances increase, many traditional manual tasks have been replaced or simplified. Employment in industries such as manufacturing and mining has dropped significantly and many workers are having difficulty finding stable jobs.

Below are some relevant considerations:

  • Industry and Type of Work: The industry in which a blue collar workers in UAE. Is employee can significantly affect his or her wage. Some industries, such as construction, manufacturing, or hospitality. May offer different wages due to the demand for specific skills. Job availability, and working conditions. For example, construction workers may receive different wages depending on the type of project. They is involve in (e.g., infrastructure projects, commercial or residential buildings).
  • Skill Level and Experience: Wage differences also depend on the skill level and experience of blue collar workers in UAE. Those with specialized skills or a long work history may receive higher wages. Employee salary certifications or specific training may have an advantage in terms of wages.
  • Collective Bargaining and Unions: The presence of unions and the ability to bargain collectively can influence wage conditions. Unions can advocate for better wages and working conditions for blue collar workers in UAE.
  • Gender and Nationality: In some cases, wage differentials may also be related to gender and nationality. Women and foreign workers may face wage inequalities compared to men and local citizens.
  • Government Policies and Labor Regulations: Government policies and labor regulations in the UAE also play an important role. These can establish minimum wages, working conditions and labor rights for blue collar workers in UAE.

Gender Wage Gap Among Blue Collar Workers

Globally, the gender wage gap persists in many countries and sectors. Women often earn less than men for the same or similar work. The International Labor Organization (ILO) and other organizations have been advocating for equal pay and the elimination of gender discrimination in the workplace.

Factors Contributing to the Wage Gap:

  • Discrimination: Gender discrimination can affect wages. Women often face barriers to certain jobs or promotions.
  • Education and Training: Differences in education and training can also influence wages.
  • Traditional Gender Roles: Cultural expectations about gender roles can affect career choices and therefore wages.
  • Maternity: Career interruptions due to childbearing can affect women’s earnings.

Policies and Regulations:

  • Governments and companies can implement policies to address the wage gap. This can include equal opportunity, pay transparency and pay parental leave.
  • In some countries, labor laws have put in place to ensure equal pay.

Work Conditions for Blue Collar Workers in the UAE

In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), working conditions for blue collar workers in UAE are regulated by Federal Law No. 8 of 1980, which has been amended several times by subsequent federal laws. Below are some key aspects related to the working conditions of blue-collar workers in UAE in the UAE:

  • Scope of Application: The labor law applies to all UAE employees, whether nationals or expatriates, with some exceptions. Public sector workers, members of the police force and armed forces, domestic staff, farmers and herders are not covered by this law.
  • Employment Contracts: Employers must present the worker with an offer letter approved by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization before signing the contract. The conditions in both documents must be the same, unless the changes benefit the worker. A notice period is established for the termination of a contract, which varies from 1 to 3 months.
  • Sponsorship and Visas: Companies established in the UAE must sponsor their foreign workers. This implies being responsible for work and residence visa procedures. The relationship between employer and employee goes beyond labor obligations and has legal implications, such as the employer’s liability in case of legal problems of the employee.

Health Concerns

Manual labor often involves physically demanding tasks and exposes workers to occupational hazards. From heavy lifting to exposure to harmful chemicals, manual laborers face an increased risk of work-related injuries and health problems.

Also, blue collar workers in UAE often have limited access to benefits such as health care, retirement plans and paid leave. Many manual jobs are part-time or contract, which means workers may not be entitled to the same benefits as their counterparts in administrative professions.

For example, a janitor working for a janitorial company may not have access to health care benefits, leaving him or her vulnerable to health problems without adequate coverage.

Working Hours and Overtime Policies

Employees are entitled to one and a half days off per week, which may be accumulated in a period of 14 days. This means that, during two consecutive workweeks, employees are entitled to enjoy a full day off and an additional working hour day.

In addition, there are 14 working holidays throughout the year. These holidays are paid, which means that employees receive their normal salary even during these days off. It is important to note that these holidays are not recoverable, which means that they cannot be exchanged for other days off or accumulated for later use.

Legal Rights and Protections for Blue Collar Workers in the UAE

In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), legal rights and protections for blue collar workers in UAE are essential to ensure a fair and safe working environment. Some of the most important rights and protections are listed below:

  • Payment of wages: Manual laborers are entitled to receive fair and timely wages for their work.
  • Paid breaks: Employees must enjoy paid breaks during their workday, according to labor regulations.
  • Overtime: If a blue-collar worker in UAE works overtime or at night, he/she should receive additional compensation for this.
  • Social benefits: Workers are entitled to social benefits, such as health insurance, pensions, and other employer-provided benefits.
  • Social security affiliation: Employers must ensure that workers are affiliated with the social security system, which includes medical care, pensions and protection against occupational hazards.
  • Protection against discrimination: Blue collar workers in UAE are protected against discrimination in the workplace because of their race, religion, gender or nationality.
  • Right to file claims: If a worker believes that his or her rights have been violated, he or she has the right to file a claim with the labor authorities.
  • Family and Medical Leave: Workers may be entitled to take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave for family or medical circumstances under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA).
  • Basic Rights: In addition to these specific rights, all workers, regardless of their occupation, have basic rights. Such as a safe working environment and fair conditions.

Employment in industries such as manufacturing and mining has dropped significantly and many workers are having difficulty finding stable jobs.

Below are some relevant considerations:

  • Industry and Type of Work: The industry in which a blue collar workers in UAE. Is employee can significantly affect his or her wage. Some industries, such as construction, manufacturing, or hospitality. May offer different wages due to the demand for specific skills. Job availability, and working conditions. For example, construction workers may receive different wages depending on the type of project. They is involve in (e.g., infrastructure projects, commercial or residential buildings).
  • Skill Level and Experience: Wage differences also depend on the skill level and experience of blue collar workers in UAE. Those with specialized skills or a long work history may receive higher wages. Employee salary certifications or specific training may have an advantage in terms of wages.
  • Collective Bargaining and Unions: The presence of unions and the ability to bargain collectively can influence wage conditions. Unions can advocate for better wages and working conditions for blue collar workers in UAE.
  • Gender and Nationality: In some cases, wage differentials may also be related to gender and nationality. Women and foreign workers may face wage inequalities compared to men and local citizens.
  • Government Policies and Labor Regulations: Government policies and labor regulations in the UAE also play an important role. These can establish minimum wages, working conditions and labor rights for blue collar workers in UAE.

Gender Wage Gap Among Blue Collar Workers

Globally, the gender wage gap persists in many countries and sectors. Women often earn less than men for the same or similar work. The International Labor Organization (ILO) and other organizations have been advocating for equal pay and the elimination of gender discrimination in the workplace.

Factors Contributing to the Wage Gap:

  • Discrimination: Gender discrimination can affect wages. Women often face barriers to certain jobs or promotions.
  • Education and Training: Differences in education and training can also influence wages.
  • Traditional Gender Roles: Cultural expectations about gender roles can affect career choices and therefore wages.
  • Maternity: Career interruptions due to childbearing can affect women’s earnings.

Policies and Regulations:

  • Governments and companies can implement policies to address the wage gap. This can include equal opportunity, pay transparency and pay parental leave.
  • In some countries, labor laws have put in place to ensure equal pay.

Work Conditions for Blue Collar Workers in the UAE

In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), working conditions for blue collar workers in UAE are regulated by Federal Law No. 8 of 1980, which has been amended several times by subsequent federal laws. Below are some key aspects related to the working conditions of blue-collar workers in UAE in the UAE:

  • Scope of Application: The labor law applies to all UAE employees, whether nationals or expatriates, with some exceptions. Public sector workers, members of the police force and armed forces, domestic staff, farmers and herders are not covered by this law.
  • Employment Contracts: Employers must present the worker with an offer letter approved by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization before signing the contract. The conditions in both documents must be the same, unless the changes benefit the worker. A notice period is established for the termination of a contract, which varies from 1 to 3 months.
  • Sponsorship and Visas: Companies established in the UAE must sponsor their foreign workers. This implies being responsible for work and residence visa procedures. The relationship between employer and employee goes beyond labor obligations and has legal implications, such as the employer’s liability in case of legal problems of the employee.

Health Concerns

Manual labor often involves physically demanding tasks and exposes workers to occupational hazards. From heavy lifting to exposure to harmful chemicals, manual laborers face an increased risk of work-related injuries and health problems.

Also, blue collar workers in UAE often have limited access to benefits such as health care, retirement plans and paid leave. Many manual jobs are part-time or contract, which means workers may not be entitled to the same benefits as their counterparts in administrative professions.

For example, a janitor working for a janitorial company may not have access to health care benefits, leaving him or her vulnerable to health problems without adequate coverage.

Working Hours and Overtime Policies

Employees are entitled to one and a half days off per week, which may be accumulated in a period of 14 days. This means that, during two consecutive workweeks, employees are entitled to enjoy a full day off and an additional working hour day.

In addition, there are 14 working holidays throughout the year. These holidays are paid, which means that employees receive their normal salary even during these days off. It is important to note that these holidays are not recoverable, which means that they cannot be exchanged for other days off or accumulated for later use.

Legal Rights and Protections for Blue Collar Workers in the UAE

In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), legal rights and protections for blue collar workers in UAE are essential to ensure a fair and safe working environment. Some of the most important rights and protections are listed below:

  • Payment of wages: Manual laborers are entitled to receive fair and timely wages for their work.
  • Paid breaks: Employees must enjoy paid breaks during their workday, according to labor regulations.
  • Overtime: If a blue-collar worker in UAE works overtime or at night, he/she should receive additional compensation for this.
  • Social benefits: Workers are entitled to social benefits, such as health insurance, pensions, and other employer-provided benefits.
  • Social security affiliation: Employers must ensure that workers are affiliated with the social security system, which includes medical care, pensions and protection against occupational hazards.
  • Protection against discrimination: Blue collar workers in UAE are protected against discrimination in the workplace because of their race, religion, gender or nationality.
  • Right to file claims: If a worker believes that his or her rights have been violated, he or she has the right to file a claim with the labor authorities.
  • Family and Medical Leave: Workers may be entitled to take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave for family or medical circumstances under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA).
  • Basic Rights: In addition to these specific rights, all workers, regardless of their occupation, have basic rights. Such as a safe working environment and fair conditions.

FAQs

What is a Certificate of Employment for Workers?

A Certificate of Employment confirms a worker’s job details with their previous employer, like:

  • Role
  • Tenure, and
  • Experience

When does an employer have to issue a Certificate of Employment?

Employers must issue a certificate of employment when:

  • An employee resigns
  • Completes a contract, or
  • Formally requests one after leaving the company.

What information does a Certificate of Employment for workers include?

The UAE certificate of employment usually includes the following:

  • Employee’s name
  • Job title
  • Employment duration
  • Duties

Sometimes it also contains salary or compensation details.

Can workers get a Certificate of Employment electronically?

Many UAE companies provide digital certificates through HR portals or official email. However, it is issued upon request for convenience and speed.

How can workers correct errors in a Certificate of Employment?

Workers should contact their former HR department to correct errors in their employment certificates. For this, they need to provide valid proof of correction and request an updated certificate promptly.

 How long should a Certificate of Employment be kept?

As a worker, you should keep it permanently. The job certificate serves as vital proof of experience for future job or visa applications.
